gaps.difference: The lesson shows reshape and transpose and assigns changed shapes, but no identified question compares equal-shaped outputs to decide whether axes were exchanged.
gaps.rationale: A small counterexample would require choosing and justifying the operation; this is a foundational bridge, not a claim to cover PyTorch.

gaps.difference: The original asks the learner to modify a supplied mean function with detailed hints; no identified short standalone function-specification task combines missing-value treatment, return and edge case without a supplied solution.
gaps.rationale: A beginner-scale specification and independent checks can bridge to later full algorithmic tasks without requiring K-NN in week 1.

gaps.difference: The pinned plan specifies two choice questions and one short written question, whereas this notebook cell contains four written prompts and no choice options.
gaps.rationale: The 10-minute planned block can use the intended format without extending class time; actual completion time is unobserved.

limitations: Recorded observations are advisory declarations, not an automated assessment of lesson meaning or problem difficulty.
